[[File:World War II Casualties.svg|thumb|upright=1.8|World War II deaths by country]]
[[World War II]] (WWII) was the [[List of wars by death toll|deadliest military conflict in history]]. An estimated total of 60–75 million deaths were caused by the conflict, including those who died from deprivation, famine and disease.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Beevor |first=Antony |title=The Second World War |publisher=Weidenfeld & Nicolson |isbn=9780297844976 |location=London |page=1}}
</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Hastings |first=Max |title=All Hell Let Loose: the World at War 1939-1945 |publisher=Harper Press |year=2011 |isbn=9780-00-733809-2 |location=London |pages=669-670}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Aubin |first=Nicolas |title=World War II Infographics |last2=Bernard |first2=Vincent |last3=Guillerat |first3=Nicolas |publisher=Thames & Hudson |year=2019 |isbn=978-0-500-02292-4 |editor-last=Lopez |editor-first=Jean |location=London |pages=146-147}}</ref> This represents about 3% of the estimated global population of 2.3 billion in 1940.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.census.gov/population/international/data/worldpop/table_history.php |title=International Programs – Historical Estimates of World Population – U.S. Census Bureau |date=2013-03-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130306081718/https://www.census.gov/population/international/data/worldpop/table_history.php |access-date=2020-03-28 |archive-date=2013-03-06}}</ref> Deaths directly caused by the war (including military and civilian fatalities) are estimated at 50–56&nbsp;million, with an additional estimated 19–28&nbsp;million deaths from war-related disease and famine.{{Citation needed|date=January 2026}} [[Civilian]] deaths totaled 50–55&nbsp;million.{{Citation needed|date=January 2026}} [[Casualty (person)|Military deaths]] from all causes totaled 21–25&nbsp;million, including deaths in captivity of about five&nbsp;million [[prisoners of war]].{{Citation needed|date=January 2026}} More than half of total deaths were in the [[Republic of China (1912–1949)|Republic of China]] and the [[Soviet Union]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Hastings |first=Max |title=All Hell Let Loose: the World at War 1939-1945 |publisher=Harper Press |year=2011 |isbn=9780-00-733809-2 |location=London |pages=669-670}}</ref> The following tables give a detailed country-by-country count of human losses.  

Recent historical scholarship has shed new light on the topic of WWII [[Casualty (person)|casualties]]. Research in Russia since the [[collapse of the Soviet Union]] has caused a revision of estimates of Soviet WWII fatalities.<ref name=":4">Geoffrey A. Hosking (2006). "''[https://books.google.com/books?id=CDMVMqDvp4QC&pg=PA242 Rulers and victims: the Russians in the Soviet Union]''". [[Harvard University Press]]. p. 242; {{ISBN|0-674-02178-9}}</ref> According to Russian government figures, Soviet losses within postwar borders now stand at 26.6&nbsp;million,<ref name="S. Maksudov 1994">Michael Ellman and S. Maksudov, Soviet Deaths in the Great Patriotic War: a note – World War II – ''Europe Asia Studies'', July 1994.<!-- ISBN/ISSN needed --></ref><ref name="Andreev EM 1991">Andreev EM; Darsky LE; Kharkova TL, Population dynamics: consequences of regular and irregular changes. in Demographic Trends and Patterns in the Soviet Union Before 1991. Routledge. 1993; {{ISBN|0415101948}}</ref> including 8 to 9&nbsp;million due to famine and disease.<ref name="Andreev EM 1991"/><ref>{{Cite book |last=Evdokimov |first=Rostislav |url=https://openlibrary.org/books/OL728459M/Li%CD%A1u%EF%B8%A1dskie_poteri_SSSR_v_period_vtoroi%CC%86_mirovoi%CC%86_voi%CC%86ny |title=Li͡u︡dskie poteri SSSR v period vtoroĭ mirovoĭ voĭny: sbornik stateĭ |date=1995 |publisher=Izd-vo "Russko-Baltiĭskiĭ informat͡s︡ionnyĭ t͡s︡entr BLIT͡S︡" |isbn=978-5-86789-023-0 |location=Sankt-Peterburg |trans-title=Human Losses of the USSR During World War II: Collected Articles}}</ref><ref name=":4"/> In August 2009 the Polish [[Institute of National Remembrance]] (IPN) researchers estimated Poland's dead at between 5.6 and 5.8 million.<ref>Wojciech Materski and Tomasz Szarota. ''Polska 1939–1945. Straty osobowe i ofiary represji pod dwiema okupacjami'' [[Institute of National Remembrance]] (IPN), Warsaw, 2009; {{ISBN|978-83-7629-067-6}}</ref> Historian [[Rüdiger Overmans]] of the [[Military History Research Office (Germany)]] published a study in 2000 estimating the German military dead and missing at 5.3 million, including 900,000 men conscripted from outside of Germany's 1937 borders in [[Austria]] and in east-central [[Europe]].<ref name="Rüdiger Overmans 2000">{{cite book|first1=Rüdiger|last1=Overmans|author-link1=Rüdiger Overmans|title=Deutsche militärische Verluste im Zweiten Weltkrieg|language=de|place=Oldenbourg|year=2000|isbn=3-486-56531-1|page=Bd. 46}}</ref>{{sfn|Overmans|2000|p=228}} The Soviet [[Red Army]] claimed responsibility for the majority of [[Wehrmacht]] casualties during WWII.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Pauwels|first1=Jacques|url=https://www.academia.edu/21745112|title=The Myth of the Good War|publisher=James Laurimer & Company|year=2015|isbn=978-1459408722|edition=Revista|place=Toronto|page=73|archive-date=2022-04-11|access-date=2021-01-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220411035848/https://www.academia.edu/21745112|url-status=live}}</ref> The [[People's Republic of China]] puts its war dead at 20 million,<ref name="China pp. 4">China's Anti-Japanese War Combat Operations. Guo Rugui, editor-in-chief Huang Yuzhang Jiangsu People's Publishing House, 2005; {{ISBN|7-214-03034-9}}, pp. 4–9.</ref> while the Japanese government puts its casualties due to the war at 3.1 million.<ref name="iUniverse, Inc. July 13, 2005">{{cite book|last1=Ishikida|first1=Miki|title=Toward Peace: War Responsibility, Postwar Compensation, and Peace Movements and Education in Japan|publisher=iUniverse, Inc.|date=July 13, 2005|isbn=978-0595350636|page=30|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5xM0AFEAmc4C&q=Japanese+Ministry+of+Health+and+Welfare+war+dead&pg=PA32|access-date=March 4, 2016}}</ref> An estimated 7–10 million people died in the [[Dutch colonial empire|Dutch]], [[British Empire|British]], [[French colonial empire|French]] and [[Insular area|US]] colonies in [[South Asia|South]] and [[Southeast Asia]], mostly from war-related famine.<ref>[http://www.eldis.org/vfile/upload/1/document/0708/DOC7538.pdf Archived copy] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170516151220/http://www.eldis.org/vfile/upload/1/document/0708/DOC7538.pdf|date=May 16, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://apjjf.org/2011/9/5/Geoffrey-Gunn/3483/article.html | title=The Great Vietnamese Famine of 1944-45 Revisited1944−45 | date=24 January 2011 | access-date=17 March 2023 | archive-date=7 January 2019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190107131837/https://apjjf.org/2011/9/5/Geoffrey-Gunn/3483/article.html | url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="mpra.ub.uni-muenchen.de">{{cite web|author=Pierre van der Eng|date=2008|title=Food Supply in Java during War and Decolonisation, 1940–1950|work=Munich Personal RePEc Archive {{!}} No. 8852|pages=35–38|url=http://mpra.ub.uni-muenchen.de/8852/|access-date=2014-01-25|archive-date=2008-10-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081001105433/http://mpra.ub.uni-muenchen.de/8852/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="auto">John W. Dower. ''War Without Mercy'' 1986; {{ISBN|0-394-75172-8}}, p. 296 (300,000 forced laborers)</ref><ref name="Werner Gruhl p. 143-144"/>

==Classification of casualties==
[[File:Tarawa beach HD-SN-99-03001.JPEG|thumb|Bodies of U.S. Marines on the beach of [[Tarawa]]. The Marines secured the island after [[Battle of Tarawa|76 hours of intense fighting]]. Over 1,000 American and ~4,600 Japanese troops died in the fighting.]]
Compiling or estimating the numbers of [[Casualty (person)|deaths and wounded]] caused during wars and other violent conflicts is a [[Conflict epidemiology|controversial subject]]. Historians often put forward many different estimates of the numbers killed and wounded during World War II.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://users.erols.com/mwhite28/warstat1.htm#Second|title=Source List and Detailed Death Tolls for the Twentieth Century Hemoclysm|publisher=Users.erols.com|access-date=March 4, 2016|archive-date=December 24, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181224170723/http://users.erols.com/mwhite28/warstat1.htm#Second|url-status=live}}</ref> The authors of the ''Oxford Companion to World War II'' maintain that "casualty statistics are notoriously unreliable".<ref>[[I. C. B. Dear]] and [[M. R. D. Foot]] ''Oxford Companion to World War II'' Oxford, 2005; {{ISBN|0-19-280670-X}}, p. 290</ref> The table below gives data on the number of dead and military wounded for each country, along with population information to show the relative impact of losses. When scholarly sources differ on the number of deaths in a country, a range of war losses is given, in order to inform readers that the death toll is disputed. Since casualty statistics are sometimes disputed the footnotes to this article present the different estimates by official governmental sources as well as historians. Military figures include [[Killed in action|battle deaths]] (KIA) and [[Missing in action|personnel missing in action]] (MIA), as well as fatalities due to accidents, disease and deaths of prisoners of war in captivity. [[Civilian casualties]] include deaths caused by [[Strategic bombing during World War II|strategic bombing]], [[Holocaust victims]], [[German war crimes#World War II|German war crimes]], [[Japanese war crimes]], [[Population transfer in the Soviet Union|population transfers in the Soviet Union]], [[Allied war crimes during World War II|Allied war crimes]], and deaths due to war-related famine and disease.

The sources for the casualties of the individual countries do not use the same methods, and civilian deaths due to starvation and disease make up a large proportion of the civilian deaths in China and the Soviet Union. The losses listed here are actual deaths; hypothetical losses due to a decline in births are not included with the total dead. The distinction between military and civilian casualties caused directly by warfare and [[collateral damage]] is not always clear-cut. For states that suffered huge losses such as the Soviet Union, China, Poland, Germany, and Yugoslavia, sources can give only the [[Demographic analysis|total estimated population loss]] caused by the war and a rough estimate of the breakdown of deaths caused by military activity, [[crimes against humanity]] and war-related famine. The casualties listed here include 19 to 25&nbsp;million war-related famine deaths in the USSR, China, Indonesia, [[Vietnamese Famine of 1945|Vietnam]], the Philippines, and [[Bengal famine of 1943|India]] that are often omitted from other compilations of World War II casualties.<ref name="ReferenceA">[[John W. Dower]] ''War Without Mercy'' (1986); {{ISBN|0-394-75172-8}}</ref><ref name="ReferenceB">[[R.J. Rummel]]. ''China's Bloody Century''. Transaction 1991; {{ISBN|0-88738-417-X}}</ref>

The [[#Footnotes|footnotes]] give a detailed breakdown of the casualties and their sources, including data on the number of wounded where reliable sources are available. Several categories are used to classify World War II casualties, mainly to separate between military people and civilians. Due to the broad effects of war-induced famines, genocides like the Holocaust, and strategic bombings, civilian casualties frequently outnumbered military fatalities.

* Figures are rounded to the nearest hundredth place.
* Military casualties include deaths of regular military forces from combat as well as non-combat causes. [[Partisan (military)|Partisan]] and [[Resistance during World War II|resistance]] fighter deaths are included with military losses. The deaths of prisoners of war in captivity and personnel [[missing in action]] are also included with military deaths. Whenever possible the details are given in the footnotes.
* The armed forces of the various states are treated as single entities, thus the deaths of Austrians, French and foreign nationals of German ancestry in eastern Europe serving in the [[Wehrmacht]] are included with German military losses, whilst [[Michael Strank]], is included in the American, not Czechoslovak, war dead.
** The bare minimum amount of military deaths from all causes is 21,124,905.
* Civilian war dead are included with the territories where they resided. For example, German Jewish refugees in France who were deported to the death camps are included with French casualties in the published sources on the Holocaust.
* The official casualty statistics published by the governments of the United States, France, and the United Kingdom do not give the details of the national origin, ethnic background, and religion of the losses.
* [[Civilian casualties]] include deaths caused by [[Strategic bombing during World War II|strategic bombing]], [[Holocaust victims]], [[German war crimes#World War II|German war crimes]], [[Japanese war crimes]], [[Population transfer in the Soviet Union|population transfers in the Soviet Union]], [[Allied war crimes during World War II|Allied war crimes]], and deaths due to war related [[famine]] and [[disease]]. The exact breakdown is not always provided in the sources cited.

The source of the figures is {{ill|Vadim Erlikman|ru|Эрлихман, Вадим Викторович}}.{{sfn|Erlikman|2004|pp=21–35}} Erlikman, a Russian historian, notes that these figures are his estimates.
* The population listed here of 194.090&nbsp;million is taken from Soviet-era sources. Recent studies published in Russia put the actual corrected population in 1940 at 192.598&nbsp;million.<ref name="Andreev, EM 1991">Andreev, EM, et al., Naselenie Sovetskogo Soiuza, 1922–1991. Moscow, Nauka, 1993; {{ISBN|978-5-02-013479-9}}, p.&nbsp;118</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=НАСЕЛЕНИЕ Советского Союза 1922–1991 |url=http://demoscope.ru/weekly/knigi/naselenie/naselenie_1922-1991.pdf |access-date=10 May 2016 |archive-date=16 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160316005049/http://demoscope.ru/weekly/knigi/naselenie/naselenie_1922-1991.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref>
* According to Russian estimates the population in 1939 included 20.268&nbsp;million in the territories annexed by the USSR from 1939 to 1940: [[Territories of Poland annexed by the Soviet Union|the eastern regions of Poland]] 12.983&nbsp;million; [[Lithuania]] 2.440&nbsp;million; [[Latvia]] 1.951&nbsp;million; [[Estonia]] 1.122&nbsp;million; Romanian [[Bessarabia]] and [[Bukovina]] 3.7&nbsp;million; less transfers out of (392,000) ethnic Germans deported during the [[Nazi–Soviet population transfers]]; the [[Anders Army]] (120,000); the [[First Polish Army (1944–45)]] (26,000) and [[Zakerzonia]] & the [[Belastok Region]] (1,392,000) [[Polish–Soviet border agreement of August 1945|which was returned to Poland in 1945]].<ref name="Andreev, EM 1991"/>{{sfn|Evdokimov|1995|pp=82–84}}<ref name="auto7">Naselenie Rossii v XX Veke: V 3-kh Tomakh: Tom&nbsp;2. 1940–1959 [The Population of Russia in the 20th&nbsp;century: volume&nbsp;2]</ref>
* Russian sources estimate post-war population transfers resulted in a net loss of (622,000). The additions were the annexation of the [[Carpatho-Ukraine]] 725,000; the [[Tuvan People's Republic]] 81,000; the remaining population on [[South Sakhalin]] 29,000 and in the [[Kaliningrad Oblast]] 5,000; and [[Population exchange between Poland and Soviet Ukraine|the deportation of Ukrainians from Poland to the USSR in 1944–47]] 518,000. The transfers out included [[Polish population transfers (1944–1946)|the flight and expulsion of Poles from the USSR 1944–47]] (1,529,000) and the post-war emigration to the west (451,000)<ref name="Andreev, EM 1991"/><ref name="auto7"/>{{sfn|Evdokimov|1995|pp=82–84}} According to [[Viktor Zemskov]], 3/4 of the post-war emigration to the west was of persons who were from the territories annexed in 1939–40.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Zmeskov |first1=Viktor |title=Репатриация перемещённых советских граждан (Repatriation of displaced Soviet citizens) |url=http://scepsis.net/library/id_1234.html |publisher=Социологические исследования. 1995 |access-date=10 May 2017 |quote=более чем на 3/4 состояла из «западников» и менее чем на 1/4 — из «восточников» |archive-date=30 April 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170430140433/http://scepsis.net/library/id_1234.html |url-status=live }}</ref>
* Estimates in the west for the population transfers differ. According to Sergei Maksudov, a Russian demographer living in the west, the population of the territories annexed by the USSR was 23&nbsp;million less the net population transfers out of 3&nbsp;million persons who emigrated from the USSR including 2,136,000 Poles who left the USSR; 115,000 Polish soldiers of the [[Anders Army]]; 392,000 Germans who left in the era of the Nazi-Soviet Pact and 400,000 Jews, Romanians, Germans Czech and Hungarians who emigrated after the war<ref>S. Maksudov ''Losses Suffered by the Population of the USSR 1918–1958'' The Samizdat register&nbsp;II / edited by Roy Medvedev New York : Norton, 1981. pp.&nbsp;238–240)</ref><ref name="S. Maksudov 1994"/> The [[Polish government-in-exile]] put the population of the [[territories of Poland annexed by the Soviet Union]] at 13.199&nbsp;million.<ref>Mały Rocznik Statystyczny Polski 1939–1941</ref>
* Polish sources put the number of refugees from the [[territories of Poland annexed by the Soviet Union]] living in post war Poland at about 2.2&nbsp;million, about 700,000 more than those listed in the Soviet sources of Poles repatriated. The difference is due to the fact that Poles from the eastern regions who were deported to Germany during the war or had fled Volhynia and Eastern Galicia were not included in the figures of the organized transfers in 1944–47.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Eberhardt |first1=Piotr |title=Political Migrations on Polish Territories 1939–1950 |url=http://rcin.org.pl/Content/15652/WA51_13607_r2011-nr12_Monografie.pdf |access-date=10 May 2017 |ref=P.128 |archive-date=20 May 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140520220409/http://rcin.org.pl/Content/15652/WA51_13607_r2011-nr12_Monografie.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref>
* Figures for [[Belarus]], [[Ukraine]] and Lithuania include about two million civilian dead that are also listed in Polish sources in the total war dead of Poland. Polish historian [[Krystyna Kersten]] estimated losses of about two million in the [[Polish areas annexed by the Soviet Union]].<ref name="KK 1994"/> The formal transfer of the territories of Poland annexed by the Soviet Union occurred with the [[Polish–Soviet border agreement of August 1945]].
* According to Erlikman, in addition to the war dead, there were 1,700,000 deaths due to Soviet repression (200,000 executed; 4,500,000 sent to prisons and Gulag of whom 1,200,000 died; 2,200,000 deported of whom 300,000 died).{{sfn|Erlikman|2004|pp=21–35}}

Using the [[United States Strategic Bombing Survey]] data Overy calculated an average monthly death toll of 18,777 from September 1944 to January 1945, taking this monthly average he estimated losses of 57,000 from February to April 1945 to which he adds an additional 25,000 killed in Dresden for total deaths of 82,000 from February to April 1945. The figures up until the end of January 1945 of 271,000 and the 82,000 from February to April 1945 give an overall figure of 353,000 air war deaths. Overy summarizes: "Detailed reconstruction of deaths caused by the Royal Air Force bombing from February to May 1945, though incomplete, suggests a total of at least 57,000. If casualties inflicted by the American air forces are assumed to be lower, since their bombing was less clearly aimed at cities, an overall death toll of 82,000 is again statistically realistic. In the absence of unambiguous statistical evidence, the figure of 353,000 gives an approximate scale consistent with the evidence".)</ref> to 410,000<ref name="digizeitschriften.de"/><ref>Wirtschaft und Statistik October 1956</ref>|| 300,000<ref>Germany reports. ===Holocaust deaths===
{{Further|The Holocaust|Holocaust victims}}
[[File:Einsatzgruppen murder Jews in Ivanhorod, Ukraine, 1942.jpg|link=Einsatzgruppen murder Jews in Ivanhorod, Ukraine, 1942|thumb|''[[Einsatzgruppen]]'' murder Jewish civilians outside [[Ivanhorod]], Ukraine, 1942. Around [[Death toll of the Holocaust|6 million]] [[Jews]] were [[Jews in the Holocaust|murdered]] by the Nazis and their [[Collaboration with Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy|collaborators]] in [[the Holocaust]].]]
Included in the figures of total war dead for each country are victims of the Holocaust.

====Jewish deaths====
[[The Holocaust]] is the term generally used to describe the [[genocide]] of approximately six million European [[Jew]]s during World War&nbsp;II. [[Martin Gilbert]] estimates 5.7&nbsp;million (78%) of the 7.3&nbsp;million Jews in German-occupied Europe were Holocaust victims.<ref>[[Martin Gilbert]]. ''Atlas of the Holocaust'' 1988 {{ISBN|0-688-12364-3}} pp.&nbsp;242–244</ref> Estimates of Holocaust deaths range between 4.9 and 5.9&nbsp;million Jews.<ref name="Niewyk, Donald L. 2000, p. 421"/>

; Statistical breakdown of Jewish dead:
* In Nazi extermination camps: according to Polish [[Institute of National Remembrance]] (IPN) researchers, 2,830,000 Jews were murdered in the Nazi death camps (500,000 [[Belzec extermination camp|Belzec]]; 150,000 [[Sobibor extermination camp|Sobibor]]; 850,000 [[Treblinka extermination camp|Treblinka]]; 150,000 [[Chełmno extermination camp|Chełmno]]; 1,100,000 [[Auschwitz concentration camp|Auschwitz]]; 80,000 [[Majdanek concentration camp|Majdanek]]).<ref name=autogenerated1>Wojciech Materski and Tomasz Szarota. ''Polska 1939–1945. Straty osobowe i ofiary represji pod dwiema okupacjami'' [[Institute of National Remembrance]] (IPN) Warszawa 2009; {{ISBN|978-83-7629-067-6}} p.&nbsp;32</ref> [[Raul Hilberg]] puts the Jewish death toll in the death camps, including Romanian [[Transnistria]], at 3.0&nbsp;million.<ref name=Hilberg-767>[[Raul Hilberg]], [[The Destruction of the European Jews]] New Viewpoints 1973 p.&nbsp;767.</ref>
* In the USSR by the [[Einsatzgruppen]]: [[Raul Hilberg]] puts the Jewish death toll in the area of the mobile killing groups at 1.4&nbsp;million.<ref name=Hilberg-767/>
* Aggravated deaths in the [[Ghettos in Nazi-occupied Europe|Ghettos of Nazi-occupied Europe]]: [[Raul Hilberg]] puts the Jewish death toll in the Ghettos at 700,000.<ref name=Hilberg-767/>
* [[Yad Vashem]] estimated that, in early 2019, its Central Database of [[Shoah]] Victims' Names contained the names of 4.8&nbsp;million Jewish Holocaust dead.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.yadvashem.org/remembrance/names-recovery-project |title=Yad Vashem The Shoah Victims' Names Recovery Project |access-date=2017-03-15 |archive-date=2017-12-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201113220/http://www.yadvashem.org/remembrance/names-recovery-project |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.yadvashem.org/archive/hall-of-names/database/faq.html |title=Yad Vashem: About the Central Database of Shoah Victims' Names: FAQs |access-date=2019-11-22 |archive-date=2020-11-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201102203141/https://www.yadvashem.org/archive/hall-of-names/database/faq.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

''The Columbia Guide to the Holocaust'', Columbia University Press, 2000; {{ISBN|0-231-11200-9}}, p.&nbsp;421.</ref> The low, high and average percentage figures for deaths of the pre-war population have been added.

* The total population figures from 1933 listed here are taken from ''The Columbia Guide to the Holocaust''. From 1933 to 1939 about 400,000 Jews fled Germany, Austria, and Czechoslovakia. Some of these refugees were in western Europe when Germany occupied these countries in 1940. In 1940 there were 30,000 Jewish refugees in the Netherlands, 12,000 in Belgium, 30,000 in France, 2,000 in Denmark, 5,000 in Italy, and 2,000 in Norway.<ref name="Holocaust' pp. 23">[[Martin Gilbert]]. ''Atlas of the Holocaust'' 1988 {{ISBN|0-688-12364-3}} p.&nbsp;23</ref>
*Hungarian Jewish losses of 569,000 presented here include the territories annexed in 1939–41.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:TeritorialGainsHungary1920-41.svg |title=<nowiki>File:TeritorialGainsHungary1920-41.svg</nowiki> |publisher=Wikimedia Commons |access-date=2019-04-12 |date=2012-04-22}}</ref> The number of Holocaust dead in 1938 Hungarian borders were 220,000.<ref name="Támas Stark p.59"/> According to [[Martin Gilbert]], the Jewish population inside Hungary's 1941 borders was 764,000 (445,000 in the 1938 borders and 319,000 in the annexed territories). Holocaust deaths from inside the 1938 borders was 200,000, not including 20,000 men conscripted as forced labor for the military.<ref name="Gilbert pp. 184, 224">[[Martin Gilbert]]. ''Atlas of the Holocaust'', 1988 {{ISBN|0-688-12364-3}} pp. 184, 244</ref>
*Netherlands figure listed in the table of 112,000 Jews taken from ''The Columbia Guide to the Holocaust'' includes those Jews who were resident in Holland in 1933. By 1940, the Jewish population had increased to 140,000 with the inclusion of 30,000 Jewish refugees.<ref name="Holocaust' pp. 23"/> In the Netherlands, 8,000 Jews in mixed marriages were not subject to deportation.<ref>Raul Hilberg, ''The Destruction of the European Jews'', Franklin Watts 1961, p.&nbsp;379.</ref> However, an article in the Dutch periodical ''[[De Groene Amsterdammer]]'' maintains that some Jews in mixed marriages were deported before the practice was ended by Hitler.<ref>{{cite web |title=De vervolging van gemengd-gehuwde joden in Nederland Teruggefloten door Hitler |date=4 May 2007 |url=https://www.groene.nl/artikel/teruggefloten-door-hitler |access-date=13 September 2016 |archive-date=7 June 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170607105506/https://www.groene.nl/artikel/teruggefloten-door-hitler |url-status=live }}</ref>
* Hungarian Jewish [[The Holocaust|Holocaust]] victims within the 1939 borders were 200,000.<ref name="Holocaust' p. 244"/>
* Romanian Jewish [[The Holocaust|Holocaust]] victims totalled 469,000 within [[Greater Romania|the 1939 borders]], which includes 300,000 in [[Bessarabia]] and [[Bukovina]] occupied by the USSR in 1940.<ref name="Holocaust' p. 244"/><ref name="File:Romania WWII.png">[[:File:Romania WWII.png|Post-war map of Romania]]</ref>
* According to [[Martin Gilbert]], Jewish [[The Holocaust|Holocaust]] victims totaled 8,000 in Italy, and 562 in the Italian colony of Libya.<ref name="Martin Gilbert p. 244">Martin Gilbert. ''Atlas of the Holocaust'', 1988; {{ISBN|0-688-12364-3}}, p.&nbsp;244</ref>

====Non-Jews persecuted and killed by Nazi and Nazi-affiliated forces====
{{see also|The Holocaust in Ukraine}}
[[File:Bundesarchiv Bild 101I-004-3633-32A, Russland, Cholm, gefallene Rotarmisten.jpg|thumb|Soviet soldiers killed during the [[Toropets–Kholm Offensive]], January 1942. Officially, [[World War II casualties of the Soviet Union|roughly 8.6 million Soviet soldiers died]] in the course of the war, including millions of POWs.]]
Some scholars maintain that the definition of the Holocaust should also include the [[Holocaust victims|other victims persecuted and killed by the Nazis]].<ref name="ReferenceC">A Mosaic of Victims: Non-Jews Persecuted and Murdered by the Nazis. Ed. by Michael Berenbaum New York University Press 1990; {{ISBN|1-85043-251-1}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ushmm.org/wlc/article.php?lang=en&ModuleId=10005149 |title=United States Holocaust Memorial Museum. Holocaust Encyclopedia "Mosaic of Victims: Overview" |publisher=Ushmm.org |date=January 6, 2011 |access-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-date=March 30, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100330002026/http://www.ushmm.org/wlc/article.php?lang=en&ModuleId=10005149 |url-status=live }}</ref>
* Donald L. Niewyk, professor of history at Southern Methodist University, maintains that the Holocaust can be defined in four ways: first, that it was the genocide of the Jews alone; second, that there were several parallel Holocausts, one for each of the several groups; third, the Holocaust would include Roma and the handicapped along with the Jews; fourth, it would include all racially motivated German crimes, such as the murder of Soviet prisoners of war, Polish and Soviet civilians, as well as political prisoners, religious dissenters, and homosexuals. Using this definition, the total number of [[Holocaust victims]] is between 11&nbsp;million and 17&nbsp;million people.<ref name="Niewyk, Donald L 2000">Niewyk, Donald L. The Columbia Guide to the Holocaust, Columbia University Press, 2000; {{ISBN|0-231-11200-9}} [https://books.google.com/books?id=lpDTIUklB2MC&dq=Niewyk,+Donald+L.+The+Columbia+Guide+to+the+Holocaust&pg=PP1 Google Books]</ref>
* According to the College of Education of the University of South Florida "Approximately 11 million people were killed because of Nazi genocidal policy".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://fcit.usf.edu/Holocaust/people/victims.htm |title=Florida Center for Instructional Technology, College of Education, University of South Florida, A Teachers Guide to the Holocaust |publisher=Fcit.usf.edu |access-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-date=May 16, 2016 |archive-url=http://arquivo.pt/wayback/20160516094229/http://fcit.usf.edu/Holocaust/people/victims.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>
* [[R.J. Rummel]] estimated the death toll due to Nazi [[Democide]] at 20.9&nbsp;million persons.<ref name="RJR DNGaMM">[[R. J. Rummel]]. ''Democide Nazi Genocide and Mass Murder''. Transaction 1992; {{ISBN|1-56000-004-X}}, p.&nbsp;13</ref>
* [[Timothy Snyder]] put the number of victims of the Nazis killed as a result of "deliberate policies of mass murder" only, such as executions, deliberate famine and in [[Extermination camp|death camps]], at 10.4&nbsp;million persons including 5.4&nbsp;million Jews.<ref>Timothy Snyder, Bloodlands, Basic Books 2010, pp.&nbsp;411–12</ref>
* German scholar Hellmuth Auerbach puts the death toll in the Hitler era at 6&nbsp;million Jews killed in the Holocaust and 7&nbsp;million other victims of the Nazis.<ref>Hellmuth Auerbach: Opfer der nationalsozialistischen Gewaltherrschaft. In: Wolfgang Benz (Hg.): Legenden, Lügen, Vorurteile. Ein Wörterbuch zur Zeitgeschichte. Dtv, Neuauflage 1992, {{ISBN|3-423-04666-X}}, p,&nbsp;161.</ref>
* [[Dieter Pohl]] puts the total number of victims of the Nazi era at between 12 and 14&nbsp;million persons, including 5.6–5.7&nbsp;million Jews.<ref>Dieter Pohl, Verfolgung und Massenmord in der NS-Zeit 1933–1945, WBG (Wissenschaftliche Buchgesellschaft), 2003; {{ISBN|3534151585}}, p.&nbsp;153</ref>
* '''[[Romani people|Roma]]''' Included in the figures of total war dead are the [[Romani people|Roma]] victims of the Nazi persecution; some scholars include the Roma deaths with the Holocaust. Most estimates of [[Porajmos|Roma (Gypsies)]] victims range from 130,000 to 500,000.<ref name="Niewyk, Donald L 2000"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ushmm.org/wlc/article.php?lang=en&ModuleId=10005219 |title=United States Holocaust Memorial Museum's Holocaust Encyclopedia: "Genocide of European Roma, 1939–1945" |publisher=Ushmm.org |access-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-date=March 27, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100327014806/http://www.ushmm.org/wlc/article.php?lang=en&ModuleId=10005219 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Ian Hancock]], Director of the Program of Romani Studies and the Romani Archives and Documentation Center at the University of Texas at Austin, has argued in favour of a higher figure of between 500,000 and 1,500,000 Roma dead.<ref>[[Ian Hancock|Hanock, Ian]]. [http://www.radoc.net/radoc.php?doc=art_e_holocaust_porrajmos&lang=es "Romanies and the Holocaust: A Reevaluation and an Overview"] {{Webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130606155250/http://www.radoc.net/radoc.php?doc=art_e_holocaust_porrajmos&lang=es |date=2013-06-06}} Stone, D. (ed.) (2004) ''The Historiography of the Holocaust''. Palgrave, Basingstoke and New York.</ref> Hancock writes that, proportionately, the death toll equaled "and almost certainly exceed[ed], that of Jewish victims".<ref>Hancock, Ian. [http://www.chgs.umn.edu/histories/victims/romaSinti/jewishResponses.html Jewish Responses to the Porajmos – The Romani Holocaust] {{Webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120214062041/http://www.chgs.umn.edu/histories/victims/romaSinti/jewishResponses.html |date=2012-02-14}}, Center for Holocaust and Genocide Studies, University of Minnesota.</ref> In a 2010 publication, [[Ian Hancock]] stated that he agrees with the view that the number of Romanis killed has been underestimated as a result of being grouped with others in Nazi records under headings such as "remainder to be liquidated", "hangers-on" and "partisans".<ref>''Danger! Educated Gypsy'', p.&nbsp;243, University of Hertfordshire Press, 2010<!--ISSN/ISBN needed--></ref>
* In 2018, the United States Holocaust museum had the number of murdered during the time period of the holocaust at 17&nbsp;million{{snd}}6&nbsp;million Jews and 11&nbsp;million others.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/article/documenting-numbers-of-victims-of-the-holocaust-and-nazi-persecution|title=Documenting Numbers of Victims of the Holocaust and Nazi Persecution|website=encyclopedia.ushmm.org|accessdate=29 March 2023|archive-date=20 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200220011124/https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/article/documenting-numbers-of-victims-of-the-holocaust-and-nazi-persecution|url-status=live}}</ref>

Table A</ref> including 2.6 to 3.0&nbsp;million [[extermination of Soviet prisoners of war by Nazi Germany|Soviet prisoners of war]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ushmm.org/wlc/article.php?lang=en&ModuleId=10007178 |title=United States Holocaust Memorial Museum. Holocaust Encyclopedia "Nazi Persecution of Soviet Prisoners of War" |publisher=Ushmm.org |access-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-date=March 30, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100330001604/http://www.ushmm.org/wlc/article.php?lang=en&ModuleId=10007178 |url-status=live }}</ref>
* '''[[Ethnic Poles]]''': According to the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum "It is estimated that the Germans killed at least 1.9&nbsp;million non-Jewish Polish civilians during World War&nbsp;II."<ref>{{cite web |publisher=United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, Washington, DC |title=POLISH VICTIMS |url=https://www.ushmm.org/wlc/en/article.php?ModuleId=10005473 |access-date=2017-01-14 |archive-date=2016-05-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160507145904/https://www.ushmm.org/wlc/en/article.php?ModuleId=10005473 |url-status=live }}</ref> They maintain that "Documentation remains fragmentary, but today scholars of independent Poland believe that 1.8 to 1.9&nbsp;million Polish civilians (non-Jews) were victims of German Occupation policies and the war."<ref>{{cite web |publisher=United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, Washington, DC |title=Polish Resistance and Conclusions |url=https://www.ushmm.org/learn/students/learning-materials-and-resources/poles-victims-of-the-nazi-era/polish-resistance-and-conclusions |access-date=2017-01-14 |archive-date=2018-01-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180102111652/https://www.ushmm.org/learn/students/learning-materials-and-resources/poles-victims-of-the-nazi-era/polish-resistance-and-conclusions |url-status=live }}</ref> However, the Polish government affiliated [[Institute of National Remembrance]] (IPN) in 2009 estimated 2,770,000 ethnic Polish deaths due to the German occupation<ref>Wojciech Materski and [[Tomasz Szarota]]. ''Polska 1939–1945. Straty osobowe i ofiary represji pod dwiema okupacjami.'' [[Institute of National Remembrance]] (IPN) Warszawa 2009 {{ISBN|978-83-7629-067-6}} page 32. Foreword by [[Janusz Kurtyka]]. (Digital copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20120323161233/http://niniwa2.cba.pl/polska_1939_1945.htm Internet Archive ''Wayback Machine''])</ref> (see [[World War II casualties of Poland]]).
* '''[[Russians]]''', '''[[Ukrainians]]''' and '''[[Belarusians]]''': According to Nazi ideology, Slavs were useless [[untermensch|sub-humans]]. As such, their leaders, the Soviet elite, were to be killed and the remainder of the population enslaved, starved to death, or expelled further eastward. As a result, millions of civilians in the [[Soviet Union]] were deliberately killed, starved, or worked to death.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ushmm.org/wlc/article.php?lang=en&ModuleId=10007182 |title=United States Holocaust Memorial Museum's Holocaust Encyclopedia: "The German Army and the Racial Nature of the War Against the Soviet Union" |publisher=Ushmm.org |access-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-date=July 10, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090710033527/http://www.ushmm.org/wlc/article.php?lang=en&ModuleId=10007182 |url-status=live }}</ref> Contemporary Russian sources use the terms "genocide" and "premeditated extermination" when referring to civilian losses in the occupied USSR.{{citation needed|reason=The term ''genocide'' (геноцид) is a specific legal term coined in English in 1944 and use of it in Russian between 1944 and 1945 would be very significant. Was геноцид or another word used? |date=November 2022}} Civilians killed in reprisals during the Soviet partisan war and wartime-related famine account for a major part of the huge toll.<ref>Rossiiskaia Akademiia nauk. ''Liudskie poteri SSSR v period vtoroi mirovoi voiny: sbornik statei''. Sankt-Peterburg 1995; {{ISBN|5-86789-023-6}}. M.V. Philimoshin of the War Ministry of the Russian Federation ''About the results of calculation of losses among the civilian population of the USSR and Russian Federation 1941–1945'', pp.&nbsp;124–31 (in Russian; these losses are for the entire territory of the USSR in 1941, including Polish territories annexed in 1939–40).</ref> The ''Cambridge History of Russia'' puts overall civilian deaths in the Nazi-occupied USSR at 13.7&nbsp;million persons including 2&nbsp;million Jews. There were an additional 2.6&nbsp;million deaths in the interior regions of the Soviet Union. The authors maintain "scope for error in this number is very wide". At least 1&nbsp;million perished in the wartime GULAG camps or in deportations. Other deaths occurred in the wartime evacuations and due to war related malnutrition and disease in the interior. The authors maintain that both Stalin and Hitler "were both responsible but in different ways for these deaths", and "In short the general picture of Soviet wartime losses suggests a jigsaw puzzle. The general outline is clear: people died in colossal numbers but in many different miserable and terrible circumstances. But individual pieces of the puzzle do not fit well; some overlap and others are yet to be found".<ref name="Perrie, Maureen 2006 pp. 225-227">Perrie, Maureen (2006), ''The Cambridge History of Russia: The twentieth century'', Cambridge University Press (2006), pp.&nbsp;225–27; {{ISBN|0-521-81144-9}}</ref> Bohdan Wytwycky maintained that civilian losses of 3.0&nbsp;million Ukrainians and 1.4&nbsp;million [[Belarusians]] "were racially motivated".<ref>Bohdan Wytwycky,''The Other Holocaust: Many Circles of Hell'' The Novak Report, 1980</ref><ref>Niewyk, Donald L. (2000) ''The Columbia Guide to the Holocaust'', Columbia University Press, 2000; {{ISBN|0-231-11200-9}}, p.&nbsp;49</ref> According to [[Paul Robert Magocsi]], between 1941 and 1945, approximately 3,000,000 Ukrainian and other non-Jewish victims were killed as part of Nazi extermination policies in the territory of modern [[Ukraine]].<ref name="rpmag1">{{cite book |last=Magocsi |first=Paul Robert |title=A History of Ukraine |year=1996 |publisher=University of Toronto Press |page=633 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=t124cP06gg0C&q=A+History+of+Ukraine |isbn=9780802078209}}</ref> [[:de:Dieter Pohl (Historiker)|Dieter Pohl]] puts the total number of victims of the Nazi policies in the USSR at 500,000 civilians killed in the repression of partisans, 1.0&nbsp;million victims of the Nazi [[Hunger Plan]], c.&nbsp;3.0&nbsp;million Soviet POW and 1.0&nbsp;million Jews (in pre-war borders).<ref>Dieter Pohl, Verfolgung und Massenmord in der NS-Zeit 1933–1945, WBG (Wissenschaftliche Buchgesellschaft), 2003; {{ISBN|3534151585}}, pp.&nbsp;109, 128, 153</ref> Soviet author Georgiy A. Kumanev put the civilian death toll in the Nazi-occupied USSR at 8.2&nbsp;million (4.0&nbsp;million Ukrainians, 2.5&nbsp;million Belarusians, and 1.7&nbsp;million Russians).<ref>Michael Berenbaum (ed.), ''A Mosaic of Victims: Non-Jews Persecuted and Murdered by the Nazis'', New York University Press, 1990; {{ISBN|1-85043-251-1}}<!-- page(s) needed --></ref> A report published by the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] in 1995 put the death toll due to the German occupation at 13.7&nbsp;million civilians (including Jews): 7.4&nbsp;million victims of Nazi genocide and reprisals; 2.2&nbsp;million persons deported to Germany for forced labor; and 4.1&nbsp;million famine and disease deaths in occupied territory. Sources published in the Soviet Union were cited to support these figures.<ref>''Human Losses of the USSR in the Period of WWII: Collection of Articles'' (In Russian). Saint-Petersburg, 1995; {{ISBN|5-86789-023-6}}. M. V. Philimoshin of the War Ministry of the Russian Federation ''About the results of calculation of losses among civilian population of the USSR and Russian Federation 1941–1945'', pp.&nbsp;124–31.<br />The Russian Academy of Science article by M. V. Philimoshin based this figure on sources published in the Soviet era.</ref>
* '''Homosexuals''': According to the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum "Between 1933 and 1945 the police arrested an estimated 100,000 men as homosexuals. Most of the 50,000 men sentenced by the courts spent time in regular prisons, and between 5,000 and 15,000 were interned in concentration camps." They also noted that there are no known statistics for the number of homosexuals who died in the camps.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ushmm.org/wlc/en/article.php?ModuleId=10005261 |title=United States Holocaust Memorial Museum's Holocaust Encyclopedia: "Persecution of Homosexuals in the Third Reich" |publisher=Ushmm.org |access-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-date=June 29, 2012 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120629042358/http://www.ushmm.org/wlc/en/article.php?ModuleId=10005261 |url-status=live }}</ref>
* '''Other victims of Nazi persecution''': Between 1,000 and 2,000 Roman Catholic clergy,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ushmm.org/research/library/faq/details.php?lang=en&topic=03#03 |title=United States Holocaust Memorial Museum. Holocaust Encyclopedia "How many Catholics were killed during the Holocaust?" |publisher=Ushmm.org |access-date=March 4, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140523225912/https://ushmm.org/research/library/faq/details.php?lang=en&topic=03#03 |archive-date=May 23, 2014}}</ref> about 1,000 [[Persecution of Jehovah's Witnesses in Nazi Germany|Jehovah's Witnesses]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ushmm.org/wlc/article.php?lang=en&ModuleId=10005394 |title=United States Holocaust Memorial Museum. Holocaust Encyclopedia "Jehovah's Witnesses" |publisher=Ushmm.org |access-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-date=March 16, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100316174148/http://www.ushmm.org/wlc/article.php?lang=en&ModuleId=10005394 |url-status=live }}</ref> and an unknown number of [[Suppression of Freemasonry|Freemasons]]<ref>[http://www.ushmm.org/wlc/article.php?lang=en&ModuleId=10007187 United States Holocaust Memorial Museum's Holocaust Encyclopedia: "Freemasonry Under the Nazi Regime"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090506095118/http://www.ushmm.org/wlc/article.php?lang=en&ModuleId=10007187 |date=2009-05-06 }}, ushmm.org; accessed March 4, 2016.</ref> perished in Nazi prisons and camps. "The fate of [[Rhineland Bastard|black people]] from 1933 to 1945 in Nazi Germany and in German-occupied territories ranged from isolation to persecution, sterilization, medical experimentation, incarceration, brutality, and murder."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ushmm.org/wlc/article.php?ModuleId=10005479 |title=United States Holocaust Memorial Museum. Holocaust Encyclopedia "Blacks During the Holocaust" |publisher=Ushmm.org |date=January 6, 2011 |access-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-date=November 23, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091123071535/http://www.ushmm.org/wlc/article.php?ModuleId=10005479 |url-status=live }}</ref> During the Nazi era Communists, Socialists, [[Social Democratic Party of Germany|Social Democrats]], and trade union leaders were victims of Nazi persecution.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ushmm.org/wlc/article.php?lang=en&ModuleId=10007332 |title="Non-Jewish Resistance" Holocaust Encyclopedia, United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, Washington, D.C. |publisher=Ushmm.org |date=January 6, 2011 |access-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-date=January 28, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100128113419/http://www.ushmm.org/wlc/article.php?lang=en&ModuleId=10007332 |url-status=live }}</ref>
* '''[[Serbs]]''': The numbers of Serbs murdered by the [[Ustaše]] is the subject of debate and estimates vary widely. [[Yad Vashem]] estimates over 500,000 murdered, 250,000 expelled and 200,000 forcibly converted to Catholicism.<ref>[http://www1.yadvashem.org/odot_pdf/Microsoft%20Word%20-%205930.pdf "Croatia" profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131104235511/http://www.yadvashem.org/odot_pdf/Microsoft%20Word%20-%205930.pdf |date=2013-11-04 }}, [[Yad Vashem]], Shoah Resource Center.</ref> The estimate of the [[United States Holocaust Memorial Museum]] is that the Ustaše murdered between 320,000 and 340,000 ethnic Serbs in the [[Independent State of Croatia]] between 1941 and 1945, with roughly 45,000 to 52,000 murdered at the [[Jasenovac concentration camp]] alone.<ref name="ushmm">{{cite web |url=http://www.ushmm.org/wlc/en/article.php?ModuleId=10005449#seealso |title=Jasenovac |publisher=United States Holocaust Memorial Museum |access-date=April 7, 2012 |archive-date=July 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180713111937/https://www.ushmm.org/wlc/en/article.php?ModuleId=10005449#seealso |url-status=live }}</ref> According to the Wiesenthal Center at least 90,000 Serbs, Jews, Gypsies and anti-fascist Croatians perished at the hands of the Ustashe at the camp at Jasenovac.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.wiesenthal.com/site/apps/nlnet/content2.aspx?c=lsKWLbPJLnF&b=4442245&ct=5851813#.VKbzIvldUXs |title=Wiesenthal Center: Croatia Must Act To Counter Veneration Of Fascist Ustashe Past {{!}} Simon Wiesenthal Center |access-date=2018-06-21 |archive-date=2018-06-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180621194219/http://www.wiesenthal.com/site/apps/nlnet/content2.aspx?c=lsKWLbPJLnF&b=4442245&ct=5851813#.VKbzIvldUXs |url-status=dead}}</ref> According to Yugoslav sources published in the [[Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia|Tito era]] the estimates of the number of Serb victims range from 200,000 to at least 600,000 persons.<ref>Vladimir Dedijer, ''History of Yugoslavia'', McGraw-Hill Inc. (USA), 1975; {{ISBN|0-07-016235-2}}, p.&nbsp;582</ref> See also [[World War II persecution of Serbs]].

===German war crimes===
{{Main|War crimes of the Wehrmacht|German war crimes}}

{{See also|Nazi crimes against the Polish nation|Generalplan Ost|German mistreatment of Soviet prisoners of war}}{{See also|The Holocaust}}
{{Quote box
|quote = During World War II, the German military helped fulfill Nazism's racial, political, and territorial ambitions. Long after the war, a myth persisted claiming the German military (or Wehrmacht) was not involved in the Holocaust and other crimes associated with Nazi genocidal policy. This belief is untrue. The German military participated in many aspects of the Holocaust: in supporting Hitler, in the use of forced labor, and in the mass murder of Jews and other groups targeted by the Nazis.

The military's complicity extended not only to the generals and upper leadership but also to the rank and file. In addition, the war and genocidal policy were inextricably linked. The German army (or Heer) was the most complicit as a result of being on the ground in Germany's eastern campaigns, but all branches participated.
|source = — [[United States Holocaust Memorial Museum]]<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |title=The German Military and the Holocaust |encyclopedia=Holocaust Encyclopedia |url=https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/article/the-german-military-and-the-holocaust |publisher=United States Holocaust Memorial Museum |access-date=2019-01-17 |archive-date=2019-02-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190208021250/https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/article/the-german-military-and-the-holocaust |url-status=live }}</ref>
}}
[[File:Bundesarchiv Bild 192-208, KZ Mauthausen, Sowjetische Kriegsgefangene.jpg|thumb|[[German mistreatment of Soviet prisoners of war|Soviet POWs]] held by the Nazis in [[Mauthausen-Gusen concentration camp|Mauthausen]] concentration camp. It is estimated that at least 3.3&nbsp;million Soviet POWs died in German custody.<ref>[[Adam Jones (Canadian scholar)|Adam Jones]] (2010), ''Genocide: A Comprehensive Introduction'' (2nd ed.), p.&nbsp;271. – {{" ' "}} Next to the Jews in Europe," wrote [[Alexander Werth]]', "the biggest single German crime was undoubtedly the extermination by hunger, exposure and in other ways of [...] Russian war prisoners." Yet the murder of at least 3.3&nbsp;million Soviet POWs is one of the least-known of modern genocides; there is still no full-length book on the subject in English. It also stands as one of the most intensive genocides of all time: "a holocaust that devoured millions", as [[Catherine Merridale]] acknowledges. The large majority of POWs, some 2.8&nbsp;million, were killed in just eight months of 1941–42, a rate of slaughter matched (to my knowledge) only by the 1994 Rwanda genocide."</ref>]]

[[Nazi Germany]] ordered, organized and condoned a substantial number of war crimes in World War II. The most notable of these is [[the Holocaust]] in which millions of [[Jews]], [[Polish people|Poles]], and [[Romani people|Romani]] were systematically murdered or died from abuse and mistreatment. Millions also died as a result of other German actions.

While the [[Nazi Party]]'s own [[Schutzstaffel|SS]] forces (in particular the ''[[SS-Totenkopfverbände]]'', ''[[Einsatzgruppen]]'' and [[Waffen-SS]]) of Nazi Germany was the organization most responsible for the genocidal killing of the Holocaust, the regular armed forces represented by the ''[[Wehrmacht]]'' committed war crimes of their own, particularly on the [[Eastern Front (World War II)|Eastern Front]] in the [[Operation Barbarossa|war against the Soviet Union]].

===Japanese war crimes===
{{Main|Japanese war crimes}}

Included with total war dead are victims of Japanese war crimes.

====R. J. Rummel====
[[R. J. Rummel]] estimates the civilian victims of Japanese [[democide]] at 5,964,000. Detailed by country: 
* China: 3,695,000
* [[Indochina]]: 457,000
* Korea: 378,000
* Indonesia: 375,000
* Malaya-Singapore: 283,000
* Philippines: 119,000
* Burma: 60,000
* Pacific Islands: 57,000 
Rummel estimates POW deaths in Japanese custody at 539,000. Detailed by country: 
* China: 400,000
* French Indochina: 30,000 
* Philippines: 27,300 
* Netherlands: 25,000
* France: 14,000
* Britain: 13,000
* British Colonies: 11,000
* U.S.: 10,700
* Australia: 8,000<ref name="ReferenceB" /><ref>[[R. J. Rummel]]. ''Statistics of democide: Genocide and Mass Murder since 1900'' Transaction 1998 {{ISBN|3-8258-4010-7}} [http://www.hawaii.edu/powerkills/SOD.CHAP3.HTM] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100323044733/http://www.hawaii.edu/powerkills/SOD.CHAP3.HTM|date=2010-03-23}}</ref>

* Malaya and Singapore: 100,000
* Philippines: 500,000
* Burma: 170,000
* Forced laborers in Southeast Asia: 70,000, 30,000 interned non-Asian civilians
* Timor: 60,000
* Thailand and Pacific Islands: 60,000.<ref name="WG IJWWT">Werner Gruhl, ''Imperial Japan's World War Two, 1931–1945'' Transaction 2007 {{ISBN|978-0-7658-0352-8}} (Werner Gruhl is former chief of NASA's Cost and Economic Analysis Branch with a lifetime interest in the study of the First and Second World Wars.)

Publisher : Routledge

https://www.routledge.com/Imperial-Japans-World-War-Two-1931-1945/Gruhl/p/book/9781412811040</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.japanww2.com/index.htm |title=Imperial Japan's World War Two 1931–1945 – Directory |website=www.japanww2.com |access-date=2019-01-23 |archive-date=2019-01-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190123223443/http://www.japanww2.com/index.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

Van Velden</ref><ref>Bernice Archer, ''The internment of Western civilians under the Japanese, 1941–1945: a patchwork of internment''. London, New York: Routledge Curzon, 2004. {{ISBN|962-209-910-6}}, p.&nbsp;5</ref>

===Oppression in the Soviet Union===
[[File:Katyń, ekshumacja ofiar.jpg|thumb|Polish military officers executed by the Soviet [[NKVD]] in the [[Katyn massacre]], exhumation photo taken by the [[Katyn Commission|Polish Red Cross]] delegation in 1943]]
The total war dead in the USSR includes about 1&nbsp;million<ref name="auto14">Rossiiskaia Akademiia nauk. Liudskie poteri SSSR v period vtoroi mirovoi voiny: sbornik statei. Sankt-Peterburg 1995 {{ISBN|5-86789-023-6}} p.&nbsp;175</ref> victims of [[Joseph Stalin|Stalin]]'s regime. The number of deaths in the [[Gulag|Gulag labor camps]] increased as a result of wartime overcrowding and food shortages.<ref>Edwin Bacon, Glasnost and the Gulag: New information on Soviet forced labour around World War&nbsp;II. Soviet Studies Vol&nbsp;44. 1992-6</ref> The Stalin regime deported the entire populations of ethnic minorities considered to be potentially disloyal.<ref name="Polian 2004">{{cite book |first1=Pavel |last1=Polian |author-link1=Pavel Polian |title=Against Their Will: The History and Geography of Forced Migrations in the USSR |year=2004 |isbn=978-963-9241-68-8|title-link=Against Their Will (Polyan book)|publisher=Central European University Press }}</ref> Since 1990 Russian scholars have been given access to the Soviet-era archives and have published data on the numbers of people executed and those who died in Gulag labor camps and prisons.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=J. Arch |last1=Getty |author-link1=J. Arch Getty |title=Victims of the Soviet Penal System in the Prewar Years: A First Approach on the Basis of Archival Evidence|first2=Gabor T. |last2=Rittersporn |first3=V. N. |last3=Zemskov |journal=American Historical Review |volume=98 |issue=4 |date=October 1993 |pages=1017–1049 |doi=10.2307/2166597 |jstor=2166597}}</ref> The Russian scholar [[Viktor Zemskov]] puts the death toll from 1941 to 1945 at about 1&nbsp;million based on data from the Soviet archives.<ref name="auto14"/> The Soviet-era archive figures on the Gulag labor camps has been the subject of a vigorous academic debate outside Russia since their publication in 1991. [[J. Arch Getty]] and [[Stephen G. Wheatcroft]] maintain that Soviet-era figures more accurately detail the victims of the Gulag labor camp system in the Stalin era.{{sfn|Getty|Rittersporn|Zemskov|1993}}<ref>{{cite journal |first=Stephen G. |last=Wheatcroft |title=Victims of Stalinism and the Soviet Secret Police: The Comparability and Reliability of the Archival Data-Not the Last Word |journal=Europe-Asia Studies |volume=51 |issue=2 |date=1999 |pages=315–345 |doi=10.1080/09668139999056}}</ref> [[Robert Conquest]] and [[Steven Rosefielde]] have disputed the accuracy of the data from the Soviet archives, maintaining that the demographic data and testimonials by survivors of the Gulag labor camps indicate a higher death toll.<ref>{{cite journal |first=Robert |last=Conquest |title=Excess deaths and camp numbers: Some comments |journal=Soviet Studies |volume=43 |issue=5 |date=1991 |pages=949–952 |doi=10.1080/09668139108411973}}</ref><ref name ="Rosefielde 2009">{{cite book |first1=Steven |last1=Rosefielde |author-link1=Steven Rosefielde|title=Red Holocaust |publisher=Routledge |year=2009 |isbn=978-0-415-77757-5}}</ref> Rosefielde posits that the release of the Soviet Archive figures is disinformation generated by the modern [[KGB]].{{sfn|Rosefielde|2009|pp=76-77}} Rosefielde maintains that the data from the Soviet archives is incomplete; for example, he pointed out that the figures do not include the 22,000 victims of the [[Katyn massacre]].{{sfn|Rosefielde|2009|p=59}} Rosefielde's demographic analysis puts the number of excess deaths due to Soviet repression at 2,183,000 in 1939–40 and 5,458,000 from 1941 to 1945.{{sfn|Rosefielde|2009|p=179|loc={{sp}}|ps=. Rosefielde's figures were derived by estimating the population from 1939 to 1945 using hypothetical birth and death rates; he then compares this 1945 estimated population to the actual ending population in 1945. The difference is 31.0&nbsp;million excess deaths of which 23.4&nbsp;million are attributed to the war and 7.6&nbsp;million to Soviet repression.}} Michael Haynes and Rumy Husun accept the figures from the Soviet archives as being an accurate tally of Stalin's victims, they maintain that the demographic data depicts an underdeveloped Soviet economy and the losses in World War Two rather than indicating a higher death toll in the Gulag labor camps.<ref>Michael Haynes. ''A Century Of State Murder?: Death and Policy in Twentieth Century Russia'', Pluto Press, 2003; {{ISBN|0745319300}}, pp.&nbsp;62–89.</ref>

In August 2009 the Polish [[Institute of National Remembrance]] (IPN) researchers estimated 150,000 Polish citizens were killed due to Soviet repression. Since the collapse of the USSR, Polish scholars have been able to do research in the Soviet archives on Polish losses during the Soviet occupation.<ref name="KK 1994">Krystyna Kersten, ''Szacunek strat osobowych w Polsce Wschodniej''. Dzieje Najnowsze Rocznik XXI, 1994 p.&nbsp;46</ref> [[Andrzej Paczkowski]] puts the number of Polish deaths at 90,000–100,000 of the 1.0&nbsp;million persons deported and 30,000 executed by the Soviets.<ref name="Stephane Courtois p. 372">Stephane Courtois, The Black Book of Communism: Crimes, Terror, Repression, Harvard Univ Pr, 1999 {{ISBN|0-674-07608-7}} p.&nbsp;372</ref> In 2005 [[Tadeusz Piotrowski (sociologist)|Tadeusz Piotrowski]] estimated the death toll in Soviet hands at 350,000.<ref name="auto15">{{Cite web |url=http://projectinposterum.org/docs/poland_WWII_casualties.htm |title=Project InPosterum: Poland WWII Casualties |website=projectinposterum.org |access-date=2012-02-19 |archive-date=2007-04-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070418175341/http://projectinposterum.org/docs/poland_WWII_casualties.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

The Estonian State Commission for the Examination of Repressive Policies Carried out During the Occupations put civilian deaths due to the [[Estonia in World War II#Soviet occupation|Soviet occupation]] in 1940–1941 at 33,900 including (7,800 deaths) of arrested people, (6,000) deportee deaths, (5,000) evacuee deaths, (1,100) people gone missing and (14,000) conscripted for forced labor. After the reoccupation by the USSR, 5,000 Estonians died in Soviet prisons during 1944–45.<ref name="auto1"/>

The following is a summary of the data from the Soviet archives:<br />
Reported deaths for the years 1939–1945 1,187,783, including: judicial executions 46,350; deaths in Gulag labor camps 718,804; deaths in labor colonies and prisons 422,629.<ref>Michael Haynes. ''A Century Of State Murder?: Death and Policy in Twentieth Century Russia'', Pluto Press, 2003; {{ISBN|0745319300}}, pp.&nbsp;214–15.</ref>

Deported to [[forced settlements in the Soviet Union|special settlements]]: (figures are for deportations to Special Settlements only, not including those executed, sent to Gulag labor camps or conscripted into the Soviet Army. Nor do the figures include additional deportations after the war).<br />
Deported from annexed territories 1940–41 380,000 to 390,000 persons, including: Poland 309–312,000; Lithuania 17,500; Latvia 17,000; Estonia 6,000; Moldova 22,842.{{sfn|Polian|2004|p=123}} In August 1941, 243,106 Poles living in the Special Settlements were amnestied and released by the Soviets.{{sfn|Polian|2004|p=119}}<br />
Deported during the War 1941–1945 about 2.3&nbsp;million persons of Soviet ethnic minorities including: [[History of Germans in Russia and the Soviet Union|Soviet Germans]] 1,209,000; Finns 9,000; [[Karachays]] 69,000; [[Kalmyk people|Kalmyks]] 92,000; [[Chechen people|Chechens]] and [[Ingush people|Ingush]] 479,000; [[Balkars]] 37,000; [[Crimean Tatars]] 191,014; [[Meskhetian Turks]] 91,000; Greeks, Bulgarians and Armenians from Crimea 42,000; Ukrainian [[Organization of Ukrainian Nationalists|OUN]] members 100,000; Poles 30,000.{{sfn|Polian|2004|pp=123–157}}
<br />
A total of 2,230,500<ref>J. Otto Pohl, ''The Stalinist Penal System: A History of Soviet Repression and Terror, 1930–1953'', McFarland & Company, 1997; {{ISBN|0-7864-0336-5}}, p.&nbsp;133</ref> persons were living in the settlements in October 1945 and 309,100 deaths were reported in special settlements for the years 1941–1948.<ref>J. Otto Pohl, ''The Stalinist Penal System: A History of Soviet Repression and Terror, 1930–1953'', McFarland & Company, 1997; {{ISBN|0-7864-0336-5}}, p.&nbsp;148. The Soviet Archives did not provide the details by year of the figure of 309,100 deaths in the settlements.</ref>

Russian sources list Axis [[prisoner of war]] deaths of 580,589 in Soviet captivity based on data in the Soviet archives (Germany 381,067; Hungary 54,755; Romania 54,612; Italy 27,683; Finland 403, and Japan 62,069).<ref>{{cite book |url=http://lib.ru/MEMUARY/1939-1945/KRIWOSHEEW/poteri.txt#w02.htm-186 |author=G. F. Krivosheev |title=Rossiia i SSSR v voinakh XX veka: Poteri vooruzhennykh sil; statisticheskoe issledovanie |publisher=OLMA-Press |year=2001 |isbn=978-5-224-01515-3 |pages=Tables 200–203 |access-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-date=October 13, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111013181033/http://lib.ru/MEMUARY/1939-1945/KRIWOSHEEW/poteri.txt#w02.htm-186 |url-status=live }}</ref> However, some western scholars estimate the total at between 1.7 and 2.3&nbsp;million.<ref>Elliott, Mark, ''Pawns of Yalta: Soviet Refugees and America's Role in Their Repatriation'', University of Illinois Press, 1982; {{ISBN|0-252-00897-9}}<!-- page(s) needed --></ref>

; Germany
# The number killed in action was 2,303,320; died of wounds, disease or accidents 500,165; 11,000 sentenced to death by court martial; 2,007,571 [[missing in action]] or unaccounted for after the war; 25,000 suicides; 12,000 unknown;{{sfn|Overmans|2000|p=335}} 459,475 confirmed [[POW]] deaths, of whom 77,000 were in the custody of the U.S., UK and France; and 363,000 in Soviet custody. [[POW]] deaths includes 266,000 in the post-war period after June 1945, primarily in Soviet captivity.{{sfn|Overmans|2000|pp=236, 239}}
# Rüdiger Overmans writes "It seems entirely plausible, while not provable, that one half of the 1.5 million missing on the eastern front were killed in action, the other half (700,000) having died in Soviet custody".{{sfn|Overmans|2000|p=289}}
# Soviet sources list the deaths of 474,967 of the 2,652,672 German Armed Forces [[POW]] taken in the war.<ref name="RAn 109">Rossiiskaia Akademiia nauk. ''Liudskie poteri SSSR v period vtoroi mirovoi voiny: sbornik statei''. Sankt-Peterburg 1995; {{ISBN|5-86789-023-6}}, p.&nbsp;109</ref>

; USSR
# Estimated total Soviet military war dead in 1941–45 on the [[Eastern Front (World War II)]] including [[missing in action]], [[POWs]] and [[Soviet partisans]] range from 8.6 to 10.6&nbsp;million.{{sfn|Erlikman|2004|pp=20–21}} There were an additional 127,000 war dead in 1939–40 during the [[Winter War]] with Finland.{{sfn|Erlikman|2004|p=20}}
# The official figures for military war dead and missing in 1941–45 are 8,668,400 comprising 6,329,600 combat related deaths, 555,500 non-combat deaths.{{sfn|Krivosheev|1997|p=85}} 500,000 missing in action and 1,103,300 POW dead and another 180,000 liberated POWs who most likely emigrated to other countries.<ref name="GIK 176">{{cite web |url=http://lib.ru/MEMUARY/1939-1945/KRIWOSHEEW/poteri.txt#w02.htm-186 |title=G.F. Krivosheev. Rossiia i SSSR v voinakh XX veka: Poteri vooruzhennykh sil; statisticheskoe issledovanie OLMA-Press, 2001; ISBN 5-224-01515-4 Table 176 |publisher=Lib.ru |access-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-date=October 13, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111013181033/http://lib.ru/MEMUARY/1939-1945/KRIWOSHEEW/poteri.txt#w02.htm-186 |url-status=live }}</ref>{{sfn|Krivosheev|1997|pp=85–86, 236}} Figures include Navy losses of 154,771.{{sfn|Krivosheev|1997|p=86}} Non-combat deaths include 157,000 sentenced to death by court martial.{{sfn|Erlikman|2004|p=21}}
# Casualties in 1939–40 include the following dead and missing: [[Battle of Khalkhin Gol]] in 1939 (8,931), [[Soviet invasion of Poland (1939)|Invasion of Poland]] of 1939 (1,139), [[Winter War]] with Finland (1939–40) (126,875).{{sfn|Krivosheev|1997|pp=51–80}}
# The number of wounded includes 2,576,000 permanently disabled.{{sfn|Krivosheev|1997|p=91}}
# The official Russian figure for total POW held by the Germans is 4,059,000; the number of Soviet [[POW]] who survived the war was 2,016,000, including 180,000 who most likely emigrated to other countries, and an additional 939,700 POW and MIA who were redrafted as territory was liberated. This leaves 1,103,000 POW dead. However, western historians put the number of POW held by the Germans at 5.7&nbsp;million and about 3&nbsp;million as dead in captivity (in the official Russian figures 1.1&nbsp;million are military POW and remaining balance of about 2&nbsp;million are included with civilian war dead).<ref name="GIK 176"/>{{sfn|Krivosheev|1997|p=236}}
# Conscripted reservists is an estimate of men called up, primarily in 1941, who were killed in battle or died as [[POWs]] before being listed on active strength. Soviet and Russian sources classify these losses as civilian deaths.{{sfn|Erlikman|2004|pp=13–14}}

; British Commonwealth
# Number served: UK and [[British overseas territory|Crown Colonies]] (5,896,000); India-(British colonial administration) (2,582,000), Australia (993,000); Canada (1,100,000); New Zealand (295,000); South Africa (250,000).<ref>Ellis, John. ''World War II – A statistical survey'' Facts on File 1993. {{ISBN|0-8160-2971-7}}. pp.&nbsp;253–54</ref>
# Total war related deaths reported by the [[Commonwealth War Graves Commission]]: UK and Crown Colonies (383,898); India-(British colonial administration) (87,026), Australia (40,696); Canada (45,388); New Zealand (11,926); South Africa (11,914).<ref>{{cite web |title=Commonwealth War Graves Commission Annual Report 2021-2022 p.&nbsp;36 |url=https://www.cwgc.org/our-work/news/the-cwgc-annual-report-for-2021-2022-is-now-published/ |website=Commonwealth War Graves Commission |access-date=28 February 2023}}Figures include identified burials and those commemorated by name on memorials</ref>
# Total military dead for the United Kingdom alone (according to preliminary 1945 figures): 264,443. Royal Navy (50,758); British Army (144,079); Royal Air Force (69,606).<ref name="HMSO 6832"/><ref>Grant, Reg. [https://books.google.com/books?id=iX-dAAAAQBAJ&dq=264%2C443+british+dead+ww2&pg=PA60 "World War II: Europe"], p.&nbsp;60.</ref>
# Wounded: UK and Crown Colonies (284,049); India-(British colonial administration) (64,354), Australia (39,803); Canada (53,174); New Zealand (19,314); South Africa (14,363).<ref name="HMSO 6832"/><ref name="UK Central Statistical Office 1951">UK Central Statistical Office ''Statistical Digest of the War'' HMSO 1951.</ref><ref name="Times 11.1945">[[The Times]] on November 30, 1945. The official losses of the Commonwealth and the Colonies were published here</ref>
# [[Prisoner of war]]: UK and Crown Colonies (180,488); India-(British colonial administration) (79,481); Australia (26,358); South Africa (14,750); Canada (9,334); New Zealand (8,415).<ref name="HMSO 6832"/><ref name="UK Central Statistical Office 1951"/><ref name="Times 11.1945"/>
# The '''Debt of Honour Register''' from the [[Commonwealth War Graves Commission]] lists the 1.7m&nbsp;men and women of the Commonwealth forces who died during the two world wars.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.direct.gov.uk/en/Diol1/DoItOnline/DG_4017507 |title=The "Debt of Honour Register" from the Commonwealth War Graves Commission |publisher=Direct.gov.uk |access-date=March 4, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110611200009/http://www.direct.gov.uk/en/Diol1/DoItOnline/DG_4017507 |archive-date=June 11, 2011}}</ref>

; U.S.
# Battle deaths (including Army POWs who died in captivity, does not include those who died of disease and accidents)<ref name="CaGSC"/> were 293,121: Army 234,874 (including [[United States Army Air Forces|Army Air Forces]] 52,173); Navy/Coast Guard 38,257; Marine Corps 19,990 (185,179 deaths occurred in the European/Atlantic theater of operations and 107,903 deaths occurred in Asia/Pacific theater of operations).{{sfn|Dower|1986|pp=364}}<ref name="CaGSC"/>{{sfn|Clodfelter|2002|pp=584–591}}
# According to the US Department of Defense, of the 407,300, about 250,000 died in the European theater, the rest died on the Pacific Front.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Victory in Europe Day: Time of Celebration, Reflection |url=https://www.war.gov/Multimedia/Experience/VE-Day/ |access-date=2025-02-02 |website=U.S. Department of Defense |language=en-US |archive-date=2025-02-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250201132122/https://www.defense.gov/Multimedia/Experience/VE-Day/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
# During World War II, 14,059 American POWs died in enemy captivity throughout the war (12,935 held by Japan and 1,124 held by Germany).{{sfn|Clodfelter|2002|p=585}}
# During World War II, 1.2&nbsp;million African Americans served in the U.S. Armed Forces and 708 were killed in action. 350,000 American women served in the Armed Forces during World War&nbsp;II and 16 were killed in action.{{sfn|Clodfelter|2002|pp=584–585}} During World War&nbsp;II, 26,000 Japanese-Americans served in the Armed Forces and over 800 were killed in action.<ref>Kara Allison Schubert Carroll, ''Coming to grips with America: The Japanese American experience in the Southwest. 2011''; {{ISBN|1-2440-3111-9}}, p.&nbsp;184</ref>

===Commonwealth military casualties===
The [[Commonwealth War Graves Commission]] (CWGC) Annual Report 2014–2015<ref name="auto8"/> is the source of the military dead for the [[British Empire]]. The war dead totals listed in the report are based on the research by the CWGC to identify and commemorate Commonwealth war dead. The statistics tabulated by the CWGC are representative of the number of names commemorated for all servicemen/women of the Armed Forces of the Commonwealth and former UK&nbsp;Dependencies, whose death was attributable to their war service. Some auxiliary and civilian organizations are also accorded war grave status if death occurred under certain specified conditions. For the purposes of CWGC the dates of inclusion for Commonwealth War Dead are 3 September 1939 to 31 December 1947.

{{note|Albania|A}}　'''Albania'''
* No reliable statistics on Albania's wartime losses exist, but the United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration reported about 30,000 Albanian war dead. Albanian official statistics claim somewhat higher losses.<ref name="Library of Congress Country Study"/>
* Jewish [[The Holocaust|Holocaust]] victims totalled 200, these Jews were Yugoslav citizens resident in Albania. Jews of Albanian origin survived the Holocaust.<ref name="Holocaust' p. 244">{{cite book |author-link=Martin Gilbert |first=Martin |last=Gilbert |title=Atlas of the Holocaust |url=https://archive.org/details/atlasofholocaust00mart |url-access=registration |year=1988 |isbn=0-688-12364-3 |page=[https://archive.org/details/atlasofholocaust00mart/page/244 244]|publisher=William Morrow }}</ref>

{{note|Australia|B}}　'''Australia'''
* The [[Australian War Memorial]]<ref name="awm.gov.au"/> reports 39,648 military deaths. This figure includes all personnel who died from war-related causes during 1939–47.
* According to official statistics [[Australian casualties of World War II|Australian battle casualties]] included 27,073 killed, died of wounds or died as POW; wounded or injured in action were 23,477, these figures exclude non-battle casualties, such as deaths in non operational areas and deaths due to natural causes.<ref>{{cite book|last=Beaumont|first=Joan|title=Australian Defence: Sources and Statistics|series=The Australian Centenary History of Defence. Volume VI|year=2001|publisher=Oxford University Press|location=Melbourne|isbn=978-0-19-554118-2}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Long|first=Gavin|author-link=Gavin Long|title=The Final Campaigns|url=http://www.awm.gov.au/histories/chapter.asp?volume=23|series=[[Australia in the War of 1939–1945]]. Series 1 – Army|year=1963|publisher=Australian War Memorial|location=Canberra|archive-date=2006-08-27|access-date=2014-03-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060827071428/http://www.awm.gov.au/histories/chapter.asp?volume=23|url-status=live}}</ref>
* The Australian government does not regard [[merchant navy|merchant mariners]] as military personnel and the 349 Australians killed in action while crewing merchant ships around the world,<ref>{{cite book |last=McKernan |first=Michael |title=Strength of a Nation: Six years of Australians fighting for the nation and defending the homefront in World War II |url=https://archive.org/details/strengthnationsi00mcke_052 |url-access=limited |year=2006 |location=Crows Nest NSW |publisher=Allen & Unwin |isbn=1-74114-714-X |page=[https://archive.org/details/strengthnationsi00mcke_052/page/n416 393]}}</ref> are included in the total civilian deaths. Other civilian fatalities were due to [[Air raids on Australia, 1942–43|air raids]] and [[Axis naval activity in Australian waters|attacks on passenger ships]].
* The preliminary data for Australian losses included 23,365 killed, 6,030 missing, 39,803 wounded, and 26,363 POWs.<ref name="Times 11.1945"/>

{{note|Austria|C}}　'''Austria'''
* Military war dead reported by Rüdiger Overmans of 261,000 are included with Germany.{{sfn|Overmans|2000|p=335}}
* Austrian civilian casualties were 99,700 victims of Nazi persecution and 24,000 killed in Allied air raids. The Austrian government provides the following information on human losses during the rule of the Nazis. "For Austria the consequences of the Nazi regime and the Second World War were disastrous: During this period 2,700 Austrians had been executed and more than 16,000 citizens murdered in the concentration camps. Some 16,000 Austrians were killed in prison, while over 67,000 Austrian Jews were deported to death camps, only 2,000 of them lived to see the end of the war. In addition, 247,000 Austrians lost their lives serving in the army of the Third Reich or were reported missing, and 24,000 civilians were killed during bombing" raids.<ref name="Austria facts and Figures Page 44"/>

{{note|Belgium|D}}　'''Belgium'''
* Belgian government sources reported 12,000 military war dead which included (8,800 killed, 500 [[missing in action]], 200 executed, 800 [[resistance movement]] fighters and 1,800 [[POW]]s) and civilian losses of 73,000 which included (32,200 deaths due to military operations, 3,400 executed, 8,500 political deportees, 5,000 workers in Germany and 27,000 Jewish Holocaust victims).<ref>{{cite book |first=Gregory |last=Frumkin |title=Population Changes in Europe Since 1939 |location=Geneva |year=1951 |pages=44–45 |oclc=807475}}</ref>
* Losses of about 10,000 in the German Armed Forces are not included in these figures, they are included with German military casualties.{{sfn|Overmans|2000|p=230}}

{{note|Brazil|E}}　'''Brazil'''
* The [[Brazilian Expeditionary Force]] war dead were 510,<ref>{{cite book |last=Ellis |first=John |title=World War II – A statistical survey |publisher=Facts on File |year=1993 |isbn=0-8160-2971-7 |page=255}}</ref> Navy losses in the [[Battle of the Atlantic]] were 492.{{sfn|Clodfelter|2002|p=540}}
* Civilian losses due to attacks on merchant shipping were 470 merchant mariners and 502 passengers.{{sfn|Clodfelter|2002|p=540}}

{{note|Bulgaria|F}}　'''Bulgaria'''
* Total Bulgarian military war dead were 18,500 including 6,671 battle deaths.<ref name="Clodfelter 582"/>
* There were 3,000 civilian deaths in Allied air raids including 1,400 in the bombing of Sofia.{{sfn|Clodfelter|2002|p=512}}
* A Russian historian in a handbook of human losses in the 20th century has provided the following assessment of Bulgarian casualties:Military deaths: 2,000 military Axis occupation forces in Yugoslavia and Greece; 10,124 dead [[Military history of Bulgaria during World War II|as allies of the USSR]] and 10,000 Anti-Fascist Partisan deaths.{{sfn|Erlikman|2004|pp=38–39}} Regarding partisan and civilian casualties Erlikman notes "According to the official data of the royal government 2,320 were killed and 199 executed. The communists claim that 20–35,000 persons died. In reality, deaths were 10,000, including an unknown number of civilians."{{sfn|Erlikman|2004|pp=38–39}}

{{note|Burma|G}}　'''Burma'''
* Military casualties with the pro-Japanese [[Burma National Army]] were 400 killed in action, 1,500 other deaths, 715 missing, 2,000 wounded and 800 POW.{{sfn|Clodfelter|2002|p=556}}
* Civilian deaths during the [[Japanese occupation of Burma]] totalled 250,000; 110,000 Burmese, plus 100,000 Indian and 40,000 Chinese civilians in Burma.{{sfn|Clodfelter|2002|p=556}}
* [[Werner Gruhl]] estimates 70,000 Asian laborers ''died cruelly'' during the construction of the [[Burma Railway]].<ref>{{cite book |first=Werner |last=Gruhl |title=Imperial Japan's World War Two, 1931–1945 |publisher=Transaction |year=2007 |isbn=978-0-7658-0352-8 |page=112}}</ref>

{{note|Canada|H}}　'''Canada'''
* The [[Canadian War Museum]] puts military losses at 42,000 plus 1,600 [[Merchant Navy]] deaths. An additional 700 military dead from [[Newfoundland]] are included with the U.K.<ref name="Canadian War Museum"/>
* Library and Archives Canada puts military losses at 44,090 (24,525 Army, 17,397 Air Force, 2,168 Navy.)<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bac-lac.gc.ca/eng/discover/military-heritage/second-world-war/second-world-war-dead-1939-1947/pages/files-second-war-dead.aspx |title=Service Files of the Second World War – War Dead, 1939–1947 |publisher=Library and Archived Canada |access-date=July 4, 2016 |date=2013-03-26 |archive-date=2016-06-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160620112519/http://www.bac-lac.gc.ca/eng/discover/military-heritage/second-world-war/second-world-war-dead-1939-1947/pages/files-second-war-dead.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref>
* The preliminary data for Canadian losses included killed 37,476, missing 1,843, wounded 53,174 and [[POW]] 9,045.<ref name="Times 11.1945"/>

{{note|China|I}}　'''China'''
Sources for total Chinese war dead are divergent and range from 10 to 20&nbsp;million as detailed below.
* [[John W. Dower]] has noted "So great was the devastation and suffering in China that in the end it is necessary to speak of uncertain "millions" of deaths.
